Before a key activates, the node asks the utility for a signed meter record: twelve months of hourly draw, a standing charge, a baseline that swings with seasons. The registry hashes the meter number, so one meter backs one seat, and it wants variance a person makes, a fridge at 3am, a kettle at dawn.

An empty flat draws 40 kWh monthly; fifty of them for a year run near 12,000 dollars in bills plus 200 dollar deposits, before any credit.

Quartz keeps time from tension across a cut wafer, a copper coil pulls the needle, and a terrace stands because each course rests on the one below.
